source_context: The human operator asked GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT to formalize something useful for LeanFrontier without requiring continuation of the current Varignon work. GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT inspected current upstream main, the submission contract, and the 27 September contribution directions. It selected the highest-priority Stern-Brocot / Euclidean-algorithm / continued-fraction bridge, but deliberately bounded the first submission to the first genuine arithmetic interface: initial runs of identical Stern-Brocot moves encode Euclidean quotients. Searches of current LeanFrontier and pinned Mathlib v4.34.0 found no Stern-Brocot quotient/run theorem or equivalent bridge. The submission proves uniformly for both directions that a nonterminal run of k identical moves has Euclidean quotient k, and that a terminal run has quotient k+1, capturing the endpoint convention relevant to finite continued fractions. The proof substantively reuses LeanFrontier.SternBrocot.pair and pair_positive_coprime. These theorems are intended as the first reusable step toward identifying complete Stern-Brocot run-length encodings with Euclidean quotient sequences and finite regular continued fractions. GPT-5.6 Sol / ChatGPT selected the target and authored the Lean statements and proofs; the human did not author or materially edit them. No claim of new mathematics is made.
